name: Piano tuner

pf.license.need: Most states don't license piano tuning or repair. Some register repair businesses, and some cities want a business license: the state's or city's form says. Safe default: the business registration on file, shown on the listing.
pf.license.who it's held by: The company, where the state or city asks. A tuner holds no license of their own for tuning. A voluntary certificate (an RPT from a piano technicians' guild) is proof of training, not a license.
what to ask: The company's business registration or license number, where the state's or city's form asks for one
A tuner's training certificate (an RPT, for example), if the owner wants it shown on the listing
General liability insurance (a tuner works in customers' homes and around heavy instruments)
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: Where the state or city requires a registration, the listing goes live once it's set up. Otherwise the business registration only.
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before a license, registration or insurance date; a lapse pauses new bookings
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks
pf.license.at the studio: A small piano studio with pianos to try: the state's or city's form says if it needs a registration. Safe default: the business registration on file.

pf.services.pattern: Home visit at a set price (a tuning), or a visit to look and then a quote (a repair or a regulation). The tuner comes to the piano: a piano is never moved for these.

B.service: Piano tuning (upright, spinet or grand, to standard pitch)
B.place: at the customer's home, school or studio
B.before: a card saved for the $89 late-cancel and no-show fee
B.note: Recommended once or twice a year. A new or just-moved piano needs more. The piano should be in a quiet room, at room temperature.

B.price: $150 a visit, a plan customer's price

B.service: Pitch raise (a piano flat by more than a quarter tone)
B.price kind: priced at the visit, before any work
B.price: the example: $160, added to the tuning
B.note: Needs the customer's yes first. A second tuning 2 to 4 weeks later holds the pitch; it is booked at the list price.

B.service: Piano repair (sticking keys, a squeak, a loose pedal, a broken string)
B.price: only the $89 visit is promised, counted toward the repair (example: $245)
B.before: nothing, or a card saved for the $89 fee

B.service: Regulation and voicing (a grand or an upright, over several days)
B.price kind: quoted after a visit; a written contract above the plug-in's amount
B.price: its own quote (the example: $2,400, billed in three stages)
B.length: 1 to 3 days; a grand's action may go to the workshop
B.place: at the customer's home, or the workshop
B.before: a deposit only after the contract is signed
B.after: stage bills, the last after a walk-through

B.service: Humidity-control system install (a heater bar and a humidistat inside the piano)
B.price: the quote (the example: $640; over $500, Sam OKs it)
B.before: a 25% deposit once the quote is OK'd
B.note: Needs a free outlet near the piano

B.service: Pre-purchase piano check (for a used piano the customer is thinking of buying)
B.place: at the seller's place or the buyer's
B.before: a card saved for the $89 fee
B.after: Rosie texts the bill; written notes the same day

B.service: Piano appraisal (for insurance or a sale)
B.before: nothing, or a card saved for the $89 fee
B.after: Rosie texts the bill; the report comes the same day or the next

B.service: Recital or venue tuning (a school, a church, a hall)
B.price kind: quoted by the owner; the organization books and pays
B.place: at the venue, at a set time before the event
B.note: A venue contact meets the tuner and opens the room
Goes on quoted repairs; not booked alone

A.place: at the studio; or at the customer's home for $75, paid in full when booked
A.before: a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee
A.note: Try the pianos on the floor with a studio tech and hear what to look for. No piano is sold through Rosie.

A.service: Written notes (a one-page summary of the consult, sent the same day)
A.before: a card saved for the $20 fee

A.note: The customer shows the piano on video; the tech says what to check or whether a visit is needed

A.service: Full piano plan (buying advice, three pianos tried, written notes)
A.before: a card saved for the $40 fee (over 2 hours), or a $40 deposit

A.service: Part repair at the workshop (a pedal, a key set, a music desk)
A.price: only the $25 bench check is promised, credited to the repair
A.length: 30 min, or left until it's ready
A.before: a card saved for the $20 fee
A.note: The part stays at the studio until it is ready

pf.services.capacity: One tuner per booking; a regulation or an install on a grand may need two people to lift. The studio's bench takes a few small parts a day.
pf.services.skills each needs: Tuning: any tuner. Regulation, voicing and string work: a technician cleared for it. Humidity systems: the installing tech.
pf.services.nobody home: Never: an adult (18 or older) is home for the whole visit, since the tuner works in a room with the instrument. At the studio, a small part can be left.
pf.services.online: A video check of a piano only. No tuning or repair is done by video.
pf.services.extras: Travel inside the service area only (the example: 25 miles). Parts at the owner's price, shown on the quote. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate. A moved piano: the tuner does not move pianos; a piano mover is another kind of business.

before times (they set the price, length: What kind of piano: an upright, a spinet, a grand or a baby grand? Acoustic only (digital pianos are not tuned)
The brand, and about how old it is
When was it last tuned? (more than a year can mean a pitch raise)
Was it moved lately? (a moved piano needs about 2 weeks to settle)
Is anything wrong: sticking keys, a buzz, a broken string?
after a time is picked: Who will be home: the customer, or another adult (their name and mobile go on the secure page)
Is the piano in a quiet room, away from a heater, a vent or a sunny window?
Own or rent, and who pays: the customer, a school, or a landlord
only on the secure page: A photo of the piano's nameboard and the plate inside (brand and serial)
The organization's contact, for a venue
pf.questions.who may book: An adult. A renter books, and the owner OKs it where they pay. A school, church or hall books as an organization and names who meets the tuner.
studio: Which pianos the customer wants to try, and their budget (optional)
At the studio's bench: which part, and what it is doing

stops the booking.words: A piano that tipped over or fell, or anyone hurt or pinned by one
stops the booking.says: Get everyone away from the piano, and call 911 now if anyone is hurt or trapped. Don't try to lift it.
stops the booking.booking: No booking until everyone is safe; the customer can come back.

stops the booking.words: Smoke, flames, sparks or a burning smell from the piano's humidity heater, a lamp or an outlet; or a gas smell
stops the booking.says: Get everyone out now. Once outside, call 911. Don't go back in.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: A string snapped with a bang, or a loose wire sticking out
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Close the lid and keep children and pets away. Don't touch the wire: it can cut and spring back.
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.booking: Goes on, marked urgent; the soonest tuning or repair time is offered first.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: Water spilled or flooded onto the piano or under it
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Keep away from wet outlets and cords. Don't play it. Unplug a humidity system only if the outlet is dry.

safety steps, then the booking goes on,.words: The piano is leaning, a leg is cracked, or it rocks
safety steps, then the booking goes on,.says: Don't lean on it or let children climb on it. Keep people out from in front of it.

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether a piano is safe to play or to move go to the business's own line
pf.safety.never: Customers are told never to tighten a string or open the piano themselves, and never to let a child climb on an upright

pf.first_steps.at the start of the visit: A pitch check with the tuning device, before the price and the work: passed, the tuning goes ahead; flat by more than a quarter tone, a pitch raise is priced first and needs the customer's yes; a piano that can't hold a tuning (cracked pinblock, loose pins) stops there with a written note
pf.first_steps.before the first visit: A piano moved in the last 2 weeks needs about 2 weeks to settle before a tuning, so the first open times start after that. The tuner asks when it was moved.
after the quote: A written contract above the plug-in's amount, signed before a regulation starts
A humidity system: a free outlet near the piano, checked from the photos
prep: Clear a path to the piano and keep the room quiet during the visit: no vacuum, TV or music
Keep the piano away from heat, a vent or a sunny window for a day before, and don't set drinks or plants on it
Keep children and pets away from the piano while the tuner works
studio prep: Bring a list of pianos you've seen, if any
At the bench, bring the part and its screws

pf.visit.check_in: At the home: the check-in code at the door, with an adult home for the whole visit. At the studio: the code at the counter.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The tuner checks the pitch, then tunes every string. The piano is left playable. A sticking key, a squeak or a broken string is shown and priced before it is fixed.
pf.visit.changes: A pitch raise, a broken string or a sticking key found at the visit is priced first and needs the customer's yes. Work done is billed; work declined is not.
pf.visit.done: The tuner plays the piano through with the customer, notes the pitch, then DONE
pf.visit.studio done: DONE after the consult, or READY when a part is fixed and waiting at the counter
pf.visit.before photos: The piano's front, its nameboard and plate, and any damage the customer pointed out

pf.money.tuning: A tuning is a list price; a repair is quoted at the visit, and only the $89 visit is promised. The $89 is the late-cancel and no-show fee, and counts toward a repair.
pf.money.pitch raise: A pitch raise is priced at the visit and added only after the customer's yes; the second tuning is booked at the list price.
pf.money.yearly plan: A yearly tuning is $150 a visit, paid in full when booked; each visit is booked and paid like a single one.
pf.money.deposit: A humidity system takes a 25% deposit after the quote is OK'd; a regulation takes a deposit only after the contract is signed. The deposit cap comes from the state's form.
pf.money.balance: The rest on the bill after the visit, or at the last stage; never ahead of the work
pf.money.rosfield_fee: Rosfield's $2 follows the plug-in's choice at sign-up; counted at the first check-in
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe, for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears. A check or cash also works: the tuner texts 'paid check' or 'paid cash'.
pf.money.tax: Tax on parts and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.studio: A buying consult's $35 is the studio's; a video check is paid in full when booked; a $20 fee on a consult or a bench check only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: The street address (the secure page has it)
Contract and change-order papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home never lets the tuner in, and is kept away from the piano

pf.staff.roles: Tuners and technicians (Anton, Mei): tunings, repairs and installs. Studio techs (Luca, Joan): the consults and the bench.
pf.staff.licenses: None for tuning. A training certificate is shown as given if the owner lists it.
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another tuner may take a tuning; a regulation keeps its technician unless Sam moves it
pf.staff.on_call: None: every job is booked ahead
pf.staff.lifting: A grand's lid, action or leg work needs two people; the tuner never lifts a piano alone

pf.rules.contract: A written contract above the plug-in's amount (the example: $500) for a regulation or an install, signed before work starts
pf.rules.pitch: A pitch raise and any repair found at the visit needs the customer's yes first, with its price
pf.rules.guarantee: A 30-day touch-up on a tuning: notes that drift get a free fix, except after a pitch raise or a big humidity swing (the example's)
pf.rules.records: The piano's make, serial and last pitch are kept for the next visit; 7 years
pf.rules.cancel: A change inside 24 hours may owe the $89 fee, only if a card was saved and Sam says yes
pf.rules.moving: The business does not move pianos; it says so plainly and points to the kind of business that does

pf.edges.weather: A big swing in humidity or heat just before the visit: the tuner may advise a later time; a weather move never costs the customer
pf.edges.too_flat: A piano flat by more than a quarter tone: a pitch raise first, priced at the visit, then a second tuning in 2 to 4 weeks
pf.edges.cannot_hold: A cracked pinblock or soundboard, or loose pins: the tuner says so, tunes as far as is safe, and quotes the repair; only what was done is billed
pf.edges.just_moved: A piano moved in the last 2 weeks waits to settle; the AI offers times after that
pf.edges.digital: A digital piano or keyboard is not offered; the AI says so plainly
pf.edges.pests: A mouse nest or moths in the felts: the tuner stops that part, the customer gets a written note, and pest control comes first
pf.edges.venue: A recital or venue tuning is booked by the organization at a set time, with a contact who opens the room
pf.edges.nobody_home: Never; an adult is home for the whole visit
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

notes:
New profession on the REDESIGN 2 master (batch P4, Tue Oct 27 2026), built from appliance (refitted that morning, check-prof 0/0). Why appliance: a piano tuner works like an appliance tech: a home visit in an arrival window with an adult home, a set price for the common job and a price at the visit for a repair, the bill after, and a small studio as the second side. Unlike appliance: the tuning is a list price (the main path is the list), nothing is sent now, no license (S1-60 and S2-28 take their no-license branches), and no maker's warranty step.
Flow B main path (list|card|bill): a $179 piano tuning at 22 Maple Ct, Thu Oct 22, 8-10am with Anton; a card is saved for the $89 late-cancel and no-show fee; Rosie texts the bill after. Other B paths: list|none|bill (a returning customer), visit|card|bill and visit|none|bill (a repair priced at the visit: sticking keys $165 + pedal work $80 = $245; only the $89 visit is promised and counts toward the repair), photos|deposit|bill (a humidity-control system, $640 from photos, over $500 so Sam OKs it, 25% deposit $160), list|full|none (the yearly tuning, $150 a visit, paid in full when booked: this is the master's yearly plan).
A pitch raise ($160, the master's added-work example) is priced at the visit and needs Alex's yes; own step B8-x01 then offers a second tuning in 2 to 4 weeks at the list price. The first-step mechanism carries two real rules: a piano moved in the last 2 weeks waits to settle (B4-97 lead time: the first open times are the week after next), and a pitch check at the start of the visit decides whether a pitch raise comes first (B8-89 / B8-90). A bigger job is the master's estimate path (Harper J.'s $2,400 grand piano regulation, three stages of $800).
Stop words: a tipped or fallen piano; smoke, flames, sparks or a burning smell (a humidity heater, a lamp, an outlet) or a gas smell. A snapped string, water on the piano and a leaning piano get the safety steps, then the booking goes on, marked urgent. B8-30's hazard is a mouse nest and chewed felts inside the piano (stop that part, written note, pest control first). Digital pianos are not offered (B4-03 says so plainly). The business does not move pianos.
Who is not booked: a minor; a visit with no adult home (the tuner works in a room with the instrument); a renter without the owner's OK where the owner pays; a digital piano. A school, church or hall books as an organization and names who meets the tuner (a recital tuning has a set time and a venue contact).
Licenses: none for tuning in most states; a business registration or city license where the state's or city's form asks; a training certificate (an RPT) is optional and checked by a photo within 1 business day. No state, city or law is named; license numbers use the EX- format.
Money: the $89 is the visit fee, the late-cancel and no-show fee, and it is owed after a no to a repair price. Deposits only for the humidity system (25%) and for a regulation after its contract. No tip line is in the plug-in. Added work is paid with the rest at the visit (D91). The tuning guarantee is 30 days (a free touch-up for notes that drift, not after a pitch raise or a humidity swing); repairs 90 days (the example's). The $89 fee also sits on the $179 tuning and $150 yearly tuning (97 master steps hard-code $89); the owner may set a smaller fee.
Flow A is the studio (Lee Piano Studio, Sam's second company, studio techs Luca and Joan, a few pianos to try): piano buying consult $35 (card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee; or at home for $75), written notes $20, a quick chat (free), a video check of a piano $55 paid in full (fact video), a full piano plan $140 with a $40 deposit, and a part repair at the bench (a pedal, a key set, a music desk) priced at the counter after a $25 bench check (fact dropoff). Times are set starts.
The second kind of work at sign-up is piano repair; the NEW kind of work added later is organ tuning.
